Actual Article Body:
Lies about Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers are becoming a bit of a national pastime in today’s political climate. In several instances, people have claimed ICE officers have engaged in monstrous behavior, only for it to be revealed later that the people making such claims were the monsters themselves. The most recent example involves Gurinder Gill, a Sacramento man who claimed ICE “disappeared” his wife but was later charged with murdering her. When informed of the alleged brutal crime, the White House condemned the incident, calling it “another ICE hoax.”

Jasmine Gill, 30, was last seen Sept. 30 and was reported missing by her cousin Oct. 4, according to reports. When local authorities questioned Gurinder Gill, he claimed that ICE officers had arrested Jasmine Gill and made her disappear while she was collecting mail at their Sacramento, California, home. The husband told the police the oft-repeated left-wing horror story of ICE officers taking innocent immigrants off the street as part of the Trump administration’s illegal immigration enforcement operations.

US Marine Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard has been indicted over the death of a Japanese woman in Naha. (Kyodo via Reuters)

Prosecutors have charged a US marine over the murder of Anna Yagi in Japan's Okinawa prefecture.

The case sparked widespread public outrage in Japan.

Officials are also reviewing the off-base code of conduct for US troops following Ms Yagi's death.

A US Marine has been charged over the murder and robbery of a woman in Japan's Okinawa prefecture while he was stationed there.

Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, stationed at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, has been accused of killing Anna Yagi in a hotel in the region's capital Naha and taking her wallet and backpack on October 3.

The 39-year-old woman appeared to have been strangled to death, according to police in local media reports.

Mr Ballard has denied the allegations.

"The case was indicted on October 25," a spokesman for the court in Naha confirmed to AFP.

The III Marine Expeditionary Force also said it was aware Mr Ballard had been charged.

"We recognise the seriousness of the charges and will continue to cooperate fully with Japanese authorities in their ongoing investigation as the legal process moves forward," it said in a statement.

Crimes including rapes, assaults, hit-and-runs and drunk driving by US military personnel have long triggered protests on the southern Japanese island, which has for years urged other regions in the country to share the burden of hosting US troops.

Japanese police arrest a 20-year-old US marine in the Okinawa prefecture on suspicion of robbing and murdering a local woman.

Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi has said that officials were reviewing the off-base code of conduct for US troops following Ms Yagi's death.

The high-level bilateral consultations will examine off-duty conduct and the "liberty" policy governing off-base private activities of US military personnel, he said.

The existing policy, updated in 2024 following a string of sexual assaults by US military personnel in Okinawa, includes a ban on US military personnel drinking in public off base between 1am and 5am or going to bars during those hours.

The US military enacted a two-day operational pause after the Marine's arrest to reinforce discipline and standards, followed by a month-long curfew.

The United States has around 54,000 military personnel stationed in Japan, mostly on Okinawa.

AFP/Reuters

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A missing mom whose rotting body was found buried in a shallow grave on a Queens beach over the weekend was shot repeatedly – and investigators believe she may have known her killer, cops and sources said Monday.

Seraphina Pereira, 35, was last seen around 11 a.m. last Monday leaving her Beach 54th Street home — about a half-mile from Rockaway Community Park in Edgemere, where her body was found wrapped in a blanket in a shallow hole five days later, police said.

Her remains were already decomposing in the pit when police descended on the scene around 9:45 p.m. Saturday, law-enforcement sources added.

Pereira had suffered gunshot wounds to the head, neck and torso, and her death was ruled a homicide, according to the city medical examiner’s office.

The Queens mom frequently posted about her children on Facebook — most recently sharing a 5th birthday post for her son, just days before her disappearance.

About a week earlier, she shared a selfie with her “lil diva” daughter, who she said did her make-up, as both posed in green eye shadow.

No arrests had been made in connection to Pereira’s death by Monday and an investigation was underway.
